service: cmd/vibeshell run (real SSH listener, real OpenCode Go provider)

steps.observed: the live generation engine produced a line-based interactive todo app; the shell kept it foreground and rendered its own continuation prompt
Added todo 1: write the live test
[ ] 1. write the live test (the item added on the previous line is still there)
the app printed 'Goodbye.' and returned the session to the shell

transcript_excerpt: Unknown command: todo. Type 'help' for commands.
todo> add write the live test
Added todo 1: write the live test
verified: an unknown command over real SSH reached the live generation engine and produced a line-based interactive app
the app stayed foreground across lines with its own continuation prompt
each submitted line was delivered to the app as an input event (an app turn), not interpreted by the shell
the app's state persisted across lines: a todo added on one line appeared in the next line's list
the app's exit returned the session to the shell, and the shell prompt answered the next command
the shell's own exit words do not end the session while an app is foreground

findings.detail: The interactive generation prompt made deepseek-v4.1-flash reason ~17.3k tokens; the 16384-token budget returned empty content and the 32768-token stream exceeded the 4096-frame SSE bound. Raised to 32768 tokens and 65536 frames (ADR 0012 amendment; commits dd85f1c, 5cf7cc6).

The SSH handler ended the session on exit/quit/logout regardless of the foreground owner, so the app's 'quit' closed the connection. Fixed so those words end the session only while the shell is foreground (commit b5c7705).

A first live app returned new_state as {session,user,shared}, which domain.AppState does not decode, so its notes were dropped between lines (add succeeded, list was empty). The generation ABI and the operator brief now name session_state/user_state/shared_state, guarded by a contract test (commit af9f7e8); the rerun above shows the todo's state persisting.

limits: one provider (OpenCode Go) and the chat protocol were exercised live; the OpenCode CLI free route served the MOTD only

the generated app treats its own invocation line ('todo --interactive') as the first app input and answers 'Unknown command: todo'; special-casing the invocation is the model's choice, not a wiring requirement
the raw transcript contains terminal control sequences from the line editor; the excerpt here is redacted and control-stripped
